name: p2m-2-dispatch-backend
description: Implement WineRix P2M-2 Core Physical Dispatch Backend as one Supabase SQL migration; backend/DB only; no commit/push/git-add.

steps.prompt: Create an isolated git worktree for the P2M-2 dispatch backend work. Repo root: {{repo_dir}} (C:\Users\F5151422\WineRix). Run from the repo root: git worktree add .worktrees/p2m-2-dispatch -b p2m-2-dispatch mainline. If the branch/worktree already exists, reuse it (git worktree list to check). Worktree path: {{worktree_path}}. Then confirm these and report what you find: {{migrations_dir}} exists; the latest existing migration is 050_sales_order_lifecycle.sql; and NO 051_*.sql file exists yet (so 051 is the free next number). Do NOT run git add, git commit, or git push. Create no files beyond what the worktree command creates. Report the migrations-dir file names and confirm 051 is free.

Produce an ordered implementation plan for WineRix P2M-2 'Core Physical Dispatch Backend' as a SINGLE new Supabase SQL migration file. Write the plan to {{plan_path}}. PLANNING ONLY - do not write the migration. All work happens in the worktree {{worktree_path}}; the migration will be created in {{migrations_dir}} as 051_<descriptive_name>.sql (confirm 051 is free first).

READ FIRST: the approved architecture {{arch_doc}}, then existing migrations in {{migrations_dir}} to copy conventions EXACTLY (do not invent patterns): 040_stock_foundation.sql (stock_items, stock_movements, movement_type CHECK which ALREADY includes 'dispatch', FOR UPDATE locking, REVOKE/GRANT, post-validation DO $$ style); 041_receive_bottling_output.sql, 042_transfer_finished_stock.sql, 043_stock_adjustments_damage.sql (SECURITY DEFINER RPC house style: search_path=public,pg_temp; FOR UPDATE locks; one ledger INSERT per location; partial-unique-index idempotency; REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC + GRANT EXECUTE TO authenticated; post-validation; assert_cellar_actor/assert_stock_admin_actor); 046_sales_orders.sql (sales_orders.status CHECK draft/confirmed/allocated/partially_allocated/ready_to_dispatch/cancelled; billing/shipping_address_snapshot JSONB; next_sales_order_number(uuid) sequence-row-locking pattern to COPY for next_dispatch_number); 047_sales_order_lines_pricing_confirmation.sql (confirm_sales_order snapshot capture; assert_sales_actor); 048_stock_allocations.sql + 049_fix_stock_allocation_rpc.sql (stock_allocations columns incl qty_bottles/status/released_at/fulfilled_at; status CHECK open/released/fulfilled/cancelled; timestamp CHECK constraints; SELECT-only RLS); 050_sales_order_lifecycle.sql (recompute_sales_order_allocation_status to mirror for recompute_sales_order_dispatch_status; cancel_sales_order which already defensively references partially_dispatched/completed); 006_tenancy_foundation.sql (organisation_members.role CHECK OWNER/ADMIN/FARM/CELLAR/SALES/VIEWER; is_org_member); 021_audit_wiring.sql + 023/028 (single audit writer public.audit_log_row_change() CASE TG_TABLE_NAME -> entity_type, fail-closed); any existing validate_<table>_org_integrity() trigger function; the updated_at trigger + immutable owner_id pattern.

DISCOVER AND RECORD in the plan the EXACT existing constraint names for sales_orders.status CHECK, stock_allocations.status CHECK, and the stock_allocations timestamp/lifecycle CHECK constraints (so they can be dropped/re-added safely preserving all existing values); the exact style of next_sales_order_number and recompute_sales_order_allocation_status; the assert_sales_actor/assert_cellar_actor bodies; the audit_log_row_change CASE structure; the validate_*_org_integrity pattern; and whether any local supabase CLI / local Postgres exists to actually apply the migration (check package.json scripts and supabase/ config) - if not, the plan must say the migration can only be verified by static review.

Enumerate, in order, every object to create/alter (dispatches table; dispatch_lines table; stock_allocations ALTER add fulfilled_qty + CHECKs and extend status CHECK to add partially_fulfilled and update lifecycle CHECKs; sales_orders status CHECK extension add partially_dispatched + completed NOT dispatched; recompute_sales_order_dispatch_status; assert_dispatch_actor; next_dispatch_number; record_dispatch RPC; audit_log_row_change CREATE OR REPLACE + triggers; cross-org integrity functions + triggers; RLS + grants; post-validation DO $$ blocks) and which existing migration each mirrors. Do NOT dismiss any requirement as already-done. Modify no file except {{plan_path}}. No commit/add/push.

Implement WineRix P2M-2 'Core Physical Dispatch Backend' as ONE new Supabase SQL migration in {{migrations_dir}}, named 051_<descriptive_name>.sql (confirm 051 is free; existing latest is 050_sales_order_lifecycle.sql). Follow the plan {{plan_path}} and the approved architecture {{arch_doc}}. All work is inside the worktree {{worktree_path}}.

ON ITERATION 1 write the full migration from scratch. ON LATER ITERATIONS first read the reviewer gate file {{review_path}} and the review markdown next to it, then fix EVERY finding; do not gratuitously rewrite working parts.

HARD SCOPE: the ONLY files you may create/modify are the single 051_*.sql migration and the implementation report {{report_path}}. Do NOT touch any React component, service, page, navigation, SalesOrderProfile.jsx, or any existing migration. Do NOT create seed/test data, dispatch UI, reports, services, Finance, invoices, payments, compliance, or void functionality. Do NOT git add/commit/push. Leave the migration uncommitted.

BUILD EXACTLY (match house style from 040-050; use the real constraint names from the plan):
1. TABLE dispatches (UUID pk, org-scoped): id, org_id, owner_id, sales_order_id (NOT NULL FK sales_orders ON DELETE RESTRICT), dispatch_number (org-scoped UNIQUE, format DISP-YYYY-NNNN), dispatched_at, status (CHECK IN ('recorded','voided') - do NOT implement void; 'voided' is future-only), address_snapshot JSONB, notes, created_at, updated_at. Full wiring: FKs to organisations+owner, indexes, RLS enabled, immutable owner_id, updated_at trigger, cross-org integrity trigger, audit trigger, grants.
2. TABLE dispatch_lines (UUID pk, org-scoped): id, org_id, owner_id, dispatch_id (FK dispatches ON DELETE CASCADE - the ONLY cascade), sales_order_id (FK RESTRICT), sales_order_line_id (FK RESTRICT), stock_allocation_id (FK RESTRICT - authoritative fulfilment link), finished_product_id (FK RESTRICT), location_id (FK RESTRICT), qty_bottles (CHECK > 0), stock_movement_id (FK stock_movements ON DELETE RESTRICT), created_at, updated_at. Full house wiring (audit AFTER INSERT at minimum, cross-org trigger, updated_at, immutable owner_id, RLS, grants). stock_movement_id: prefer NOT NULL if achievable without a circular-FK deadlock; the transaction-safe order is insert dispatch header -> insert dispatch_line -> insert stock_movement referencing dispatch_line.id -> UPDATE dispatch_line.stock_movement_id in the SAME transaction. If NOT NULL forces a nullable-at-insert problem, keep it nullable at table level but DOCUMENT in a SQL comment that record_dispatch always sets it within the same transaction. Do not weaken integrity casually.
3. ALTER stock_allocations: ADD fulfilled_qty INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK fulfilled_qty>=0 and CHECK fulfilled_qty<=qty_bottles. Extend status CHECK (open,released,fulfilled,cancelled) -> (open,partially_fulfilled,released,fulfilled,cancelled): inspect the existing constraint name (from the plan), DROP and re-ADD preserving ALL existing values. Update the existing timestamp/lifecycle CHECKs so: open => fulfilled_qty=0, released_at IS NULL, fulfilled_at IS NULL; partially_fulfilled => fulfilled_qty>0 AND fulfilled_qty<qty_bottles, released_at IS NULL, fulfilled_at IS NULL; fulfilled => fulfilled_qty=qty_bottles AND fulfilled_at IS NOT NULL AND released_at IS NULL; released/cancelled MUST remain exactly compatible with existing P2L-6 release behaviour. NEVER modify qty_bottles; never delete/recreate allocation rows. Existing rows (fulfilled_qty defaulting to 0) must stay valid.
4. ALTER sales_orders.status CHECK to ADD 'partially_dispatched' and 'completed' (NOT 'dispatched'), preserving ALL existing values. Inspect existing constraint name first.
5. FUNCTION recompute_sales_order_dispatch_status(p_sales_order_id uuid) SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public,pg_temp. Derive status from ACTUAL FULFILLED QUANTITIES (not dispatch-row counts): every line fully fulfilled (sum of its allocations' fulfilled_qty >= line qty) => 'completed'; at least one bottle fulfilled but not all => 'partially_dispatched'; zero fulfilled => leave 'ready_to_dispatch'. Lock the sales order appropriately when called inside record_dispatch. Mirror recompute_sales_order_allocation_status.
6. FUNCTION assert_dispatch_actor(target_org uuid) SECURITY DEFINER, pinned search_path, not public. Allow OWNER/ADMIN/CELLAR/SALES; reject FARM/VIEWER. Mirror assert_sales_actor/assert_cellar_actor.
7. FUNCTION next_dispatch_number(uuid) SECURITY DEFINER, pinned search_path, REVOKE PUBLIC EXECUTE, GRANT authenticated EXECUTE, org-scoped, locks the sequence row (same concurrency-safe pattern as next_sales_order_number). Format DISP-YYYY-NNNN (e.g. DISP-2026-0001). Gaps acceptable.
8. FUNCTION record_dispatch(p_sales_order_id uuid, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text default null) SECURITY DEFINER, search_path=public,pg_temp, REVOKE PUBLIC EXECUTE, GRANT authenticated EXECUTE. ATOMIC. p_lines is a jsonb array of {stock_allocation_id, qty_bottles}. Steps (one transaction; any failure RAISEs and rolls back): (1) auth.uid() not null; (2) SELECT sales_orders FOR UPDATE (derive org_id from the row - never trust client org); (3) assert_dispatch_actor(order.org_id); (4) order.status IN ('ready_to_dispatch','partially_dispatched') else RAISE; (5) p_lines non-empty jsonb array, each element integer qty_bottles>0 and a stock_allocation_id; (6) process allocations in DETERMINISTIC order (ORDER BY stock_allocation_id); per allocation SELECT stock_allocations FOR UPDATE, validate it belongs to this order, status IN ('open','partially_fulfilled'), remaining = qty_bottles - fulfilled_qty, reject if requested > remaining, DERIVE sales_order_line_id/finished_product_id/location_id FROM the locked allocation (never trust client copies - client sends only stock_allocation_id + qty); (7) SELECT the stock_items row (org_id, product_id=allocation.finished_product_id, location_id=allocation.location_id) FOR UPDATE, validate qty_bottles>=requested, decrement it; (8) create the dispatch header ONCE (next_dispatch_number, dispatched_at=now(), status='recorded', address_snapshot defaulting to the order's shipping_address_snapshot, notes=p_notes) BEFORE the lines; (9) per line INSERT dispatch_lines (deriving FK columns from the locked allocation), then INSERT stock_movements (movement_type='dispatch', qty_bottles_delta=-requested, reference_type='dispatch_line', reference_id=dispatch_line.id, product/location/org from allocation), then UPDATE dispatch_line.stock_movement_id = that movement id - ONE stock_movement per line/location, NEVER aggregated; (10) increase allocation.fulfilled_qty; set status 'fulfilled' + fulfilled_at=now() when fulfilled_qty=qty_bottles else 'partially_fulfilled' with fulfilled_at NULL; (11) call recompute_sales_order_dispatch_status(order.id); (12) return the dispatch header + useful per-line results. Do NOT manually INSERT audit_log rows (triggers do it). NEVER touch sales_order_lines.quantity_bottles. Lock order MUST be sales_orders -> stock_allocations -> stock_items, all FOR UPDATE, so a concurrent 60+60 against a 100-bottle allocation makes the second txn fail on the remaining-quantity check. No negative stock. Idempotency this phase = locking + remaining-quantity validation only (NO client idempotency key).
9. AUDIT: CREATE OR REPLACE public.audit_log_row_change() adding 'dispatches' and 'dispatch_lines' -> entity_type mappings, PRESERVING every existing WHEN branch and fail-closed behaviour; attach AFTER INSERT (and UPDATE where house style audits updates) triggers to both tables.
10. RLS: enable on both tables; SELECT policy is_org_member(org_id); NO client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies; GRANT SELECT TO authenticated only. All writes via record_dispatch.
11. CROSS-ORG: validate_dispatch_org_integrity() and validate_dispatch_line_org_integrity() SECURITY DEFINER pinned search_path, BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE triggers, verifying all referenced rows share one org. Copy the existing validate_*_org_integrity pattern.
12. FK DELETE: RESTRICT for all historical/business refs; CASCADE only dispatch_lines->dispatches. No DELETE RPC.
13. ADDRESS SNAPSHOT: dispatches.address_snapshot JSONB; RPC defaults it to the order's shipping_address_snapshot (copy, not a live FK). Never modify the sales order snapshot.
14. MIGRATION SAFETY: before each CHECK change use the real constraint name from the plan; replace preserving all existing values; preflight checks; transactional structure where appropriate; no backfill; existing allocations stay valid.
15. POST-VALIDATION DO $$ blocks (house style) verifying: both tables exist; RLS enabled; correct SELECT policies; NO direct write grants; dispatch_number uniqueness; required columns; FK count + delete behaviours; CHECK constraints; triggers (updated_at, audit, cross-org); audit mappings for both tables; next_dispatch_number exists + SECURITY DEFINER + search_path pinned + PUBLIC revoked + authenticated granted; record_dispatch same; fulfilled_qty + its constraints; stock_allocations status CHECK contains partially_fulfilled; sales_orders status CHECK contains partially_dispatched AND completed; and ASSERT stock_items still has NO column named reserved/allocated/reserved_qty/allocated_qty (and do not add one).

Then write the implementation report to {{report_path}} covering: 1 implementation summary; 2 exact migration filename; 3 objects created/modified; 4 security summary; 5 audit summary; 6 concurrency/idempotency summary; 7 post-validation results; 8 build result (run npm run build in {{repo_dir}} if practical and report the HONEST result - SQL-only change so JS build should be unaffected; if there is no local Postgres/supabase CLI to actually APPLY the migration, say so explicitly and do NOT fabricate apply results - verify SQL correctness by static review against 040-050); 9 a SINGLE consolidated Supabase SQL verification query returning one row per check with columns check_name, result, verdict ('PASS'/'FAIL') covering the key post-validation items (user runs it manually in the Supabase SQL editor); 10 a MANUAL test plan (do NOT execute, do NOT create data) - reference existing SO-2026-0001 if the agent can confirm it exists in ready_to_dispatch with allocations, else state what order/allocation characteristics are needed; test dispatch 60 then remaining 40 with expected stock 4975->4915->4875, allocation partially_fulfilled then fulfilled, order partially_dispatched then completed, asserting no negative stock / no duplicate movement / no duplicate fulfilment; 11 files changed; 12 risks/deviations.

If any instruction would force altering existing product behaviour or exceeding scope, STOP and raise it rather than doing it. No commit/add/push.

Review the P2M-2 dispatch backend migration (the single new 051_*.sql in {{migrations_dir}}, inside worktree {{worktree_path}}) against the approved architecture {{arch_doc}}, the plan {{plan_path}}, and the report {{report_path}}.

First write your full narrative review to a markdown file next to the gate JSON. Then write the machine-readable gate verdict to {{review_path}} as JSON: {"verdict":"APPROVED"} or {"verdict":"CHANGES_REQUESTED","findings":[...]}. The word APPROVED must appear in your final send_message output ONLY when you approve.

Check specifically: (a) house-style fidelity vs migrations 040-050 (SECURITY DEFINER + search_path=public,pg_temp; REVOKE PUBLIC + GRANT authenticated; FOR UPDATE locking; one ledger INSERT per location; post-validation DO $$ blocks; single audit writer extended not replaced; validate_*_org_integrity pattern; updated_at + immutable owner_id triggers); (b) CHECK-constraint surgery safety - real existing constraint names used, ALL prior allowed values preserved for sales_orders.status and stock_allocations.status and the allocation lifecycle CHECKs, and existing rows (fulfilled_qty=0, open/released/fulfilled/cancelled) remain valid; (c) record_dispatch atomicity and lock order (sales_orders -> stock_allocations -> stock_items, deterministic allocation ordering) so concurrent 60+60 on a 100-bottle allocation cannot over-dispatch and stock cannot go negative; (d) the client CANNOT smuggle org/sales_order_line/product/location - all derived from the locked allocation, order/org from the locked sales order; (e) movement_type='dispatch' reused (not 'sale', no new type), one movement per line, reference_type='dispatch_line'/reference_id=dispatch_line.id, stock_movement_id wired back in the same transaction; (f) NO second audit system and NO second physical stock ledger; sales_order_lines.quantity_bottles never modified; allocations never deleted/recreated and qty_bottles never changed; (g) scope - ONLY the one 051 migration (plus report) changed, no React/service/page/other-migration files touched, no void/Finance/compliance/seed data; (h) stock_items gained NO reserved/allocated/reserved_qty/allocated_qty column; (i) nothing committed/added/pushed. If the migration cannot be applied locally, confirm the report is HONEST about that rather than fabricating apply results. Any HIGH or MEDIUM finding => CHANGES_REQUESTED. Always end with a send_message (severity success) stating the verdict.
